newsitem.title: USA: Previously owned home sales down in March.
newsitem.headline: Previously owned home sales down in March.

text.p: Sales of previously owned homes tapered off in March as higher interest rates and bad weather dampened activity in the housing sector, a trade group said Friday.
The National Association of Realtors said that sales of existing homes fell 2.8 percent in March to a seasonably adjusted annual rate of 4.11 million units from a revised 4.23 million in February.

In February sales had jumped to their second highest level on record. The group attributed the drop in March sales to adverse weather conditions in some parts of the country and to an increase in interest rates.

"The activity we are seeing now is beginning to reflect the impact of bad weather, including massive flooding in the Midwest and West, which has diverted attention from home ownership to survival," NAR President Russell Booth said.
Booth said the March slowdown indicates that the housing market is "leveling out to a more normal pattern of activity."
The group said it did not anticipate any major swings in interest rates for the remainder of the year.
The median price of an existing home rose to $120,000 in March from $117,500 in Feburary. It was $115,700 a year ago.
Mortgage rates for a 30-year loan averaged 7.90 percent in March, up from 7.65 percent in February and 7.62 percent a year ago.
During March, sales for existing homes rose 1.6 percent in the Northeast to 640,000 a year, while in the South, the nation's biggest regional housing market, they were unchanged at 1.53 million.
In the Midwest, March sales dropped 8.3 percent to a rate of 1 million units and in the West they fell 5.1 percent to 930,000 units.
There were 2.35 million existing homes available at the end of March, representing a 6.9-month supply at the current pace.
